sentences.text: Ageleodus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Paleozoic era.
The genus is known from two species, and all known fossils consist of isolated teeth.
The species A. altus was described in 2006 based on fossils from the Carboniferous of Australia.
A study of 382 specimens revealed that Ageleodus exhibited strong heterodonty, with teeth varying widely in length and the number of cusps.
Ageleodus belongs to the parent group Holocephali and is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
This animal lived between 372.15 and 303.7 million years ago, spanning from the Famennian to the Kasimovian stages.
Although generally considered a chondrichthyan, Ageleodus has not been classified into any known order or family.
